claim: “80% of the code” means 80% of research is automated.
reason: Code attribution is not time saved, research judgment, or independently validated successor improvement.

claim: An acrostic proves DeepMind achieved runaway RSI.
reason: The supplied rumour provides no verified sequence of autonomous successor improvements.

claim: The incident proves imminent extinction.
reason: Observed unauthorised behaviour establishes a control problem; extrapolation needs further assumptions.

claim: The intrusion means Australian patient records were stolen.
reason: The official account describes a statistics portal and an ongoing investigation.

claim: The internet is now universally unsafe for training.
reason: Keep alleged persistence distinct from data poisoning, prompt injection and code execution.

claim: All proponents support the same pause.
reason: Standards, embedded evaluation, licences and capability constraints are different interventions.

claim: Hassabis categorically rules out slowing down.
reason: Read the staged framework and its potential escalation.

claim: An evaluator’s funding alone proves corrupt findings.
reason: Investigate contracts, appointments, scope, access, publication and ability to challenge results.

claim: An announcement proves independent evaluation is operational.
reason: Implementation and consequences require separate evidence.

claim: The world has measurably spent exactly $1.5tn on AI since launch.
reason: The earlier number was a straight-line interpolation of approximate forecasts.

claim: Private financing and corporate investment can be added.
reason: Private financing is included in the broader corporate series.

claim: Financing, cloud revenue, and equipment purchases are additive investment.
reason: Separate financial exposure, intermediate transactions and capital formation.

claim: A revenue run-rate is realised annual profit.
reason: Annualisation, revenue, and profit are different measures.

claim: The earlier 65% shakeout judgment is a measured risk.
reason: It combines two subjective scenarios from 19 September; no calibrated forecasting model.

claim: The dot-com analogy supplies the crash date.
reason: It suggests mechanisms, not an elapsed-time countdown.

claim: The United States has a general four-to-seven-month lead.
reason: The measured comparison is task-specific and model-specific.

claim: All open models are ten times cheaper.
reason: Use cost per successful task under matched conditions, including operations.

claim: Open weights eliminate hardware and governance constraints.
reason: Copying a model does not supply compute or settle acceptable use.

claim: China’s openness began as a response to September pacing.
reason: Published support for open ecosystems predates the proposal.

claim: Progress despite export controls proves the controls had no effect.
reason: A causal claim needs a counterfactual, not only observed progress.

claim: The September proposal caused the original military exclusion.
reason: The contract dispute and exclusion precede the essay.

claim: A procurement opinion is a general technical verdict on AI safety.
reason: The legal question and remedy are narrower.

claim: An antitrust complaint establishes an illegal agreement.
reason: A complaint contains allegations; merits findings require separate evidence.

claim: The policy scores are judgments from 51 real economists.
reason: The numerical panel uses simulated personas.

claim: Employment evidence proves paid jobs will always be necessary for meaning.
reason: Present-setting effects do not resolve fundamentally transformed institutions.

claim: Income, ownership and democratic voice are interchangeable.
reason: Material claims and decision rights require different designs.

claim: Intelligent or curious behaviour establishes subjective experience.
reason: Observable competence does not resolve consciousness.

claim: More intelligence must either abolish or entrench the State.
reason: Specify mechanisms, rights, access, and changed governance arrangements.
